text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Tuesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Central bank governor Reinoldijus Sharkinas promised a meeting of the state's defence council to impose stricter demands on banks. At the meeting, the reliability of banks was discussed in relation to national security.

- Although Lithuania's health insurance system comes into force today, the system is still working on the basis of advance payments to health care facilities rather than work performed. The new system is to be based on work completed, but the prices for medical services still have not been confirmed.
- "God sees that I am not guilty," Valeri Ivanov, the former Yedinstvo leader accused of slander, told a Vilnius court on the yesterday.

Ivanov faces slander charges for alleging that Lithuanian victims of the "January Events," when Soviet OMON agents killed 13 protestors in Vilnius in January 1991, did not die because of the actions of Soviet troops but for other reasons.
- On Monday, 1.75 percent of the share capital of Klaipedos Nafta was sold in block trading at Lithuania's stock exchange for 700,000 litas at 100 litas a share.
- Central bank governor Reinoldijus Sharkinas told a press conference that specialists had determined that Tauras Bank was insolvent.

- Central bank governor Reinoldijus Sharkinas said that Tauras Bank is "really insolvent" and that the board of the Bank of Lithuania would take the final decision concerning the troubled bank on Tuesday.

- An official with the state control department said that a search of the apartment of Genadijus Konopliovas, the Tauras Bank president who was found dead in a suspected suicide on June 23, had turned up "interesting documents" but declined to describe them.

- The state defence council, which is led by President Algirdas Brazauskas, told the agricultural and forestry ministry and the interior ministry to examine the possibility of moving the foreigners registration centre from Pabrade to another location.
- The newspaper says that the state controllers warned three times that distribution of a 17 million ECU European Union loan through Tauras Bank was suspicious.
